background_notes.justification: A sequence is Cauchy, or has difference converging to zero, in ||.|| exactly when it is so in c||.||. The induced maps on equivalence classes of Cauchy sequences are inverse and extend the identity. In the Fourier realization they have identical coefficients, hence the same distribution. For r<=s, each nonnegative weighted coefficient square for order r is bounded by that for order s. Comparison of partial sums and then their suprema gives the norm inequality, and the inclusion extends through the completions. This verifies the norm/membership bridge actually proved in S001.

background_notes.fact: For gamma>0, the Airy group is an isometry and strongly continuous on every H^s; Dinv maps mean-zero H^gamma boundedly into H^(1+gamma); Pnz is bounded there; multiplication is a continuous bilinear map on H^r for r=1+gamma>1/2. The E003 endpoint formula therefore gives continuous H^(1+gamma), and hence H^agamma, stage representatives.

background_notes.justification: Airy phases have modulus one. Strong continuity follows by convergence on any fixed finite set of modes, with the remaining square-summable tails bounded uniformly by four times the original tail. For Dinv, <k>^2/k^2<=2 when k!=0; deleting the zero coefficient cannot increase a Fourier norm. For multiplication, <k>^r<=C_r(<l>^r+<k-l>^r) bounds the weighted convolution by two ell^2-ell^1 convolutions. Their ell^2 norms are bounded by the product of the respective sequence norms, by the triangle inequality applied to translated sequences. Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||hat h||_ell^1<= (sum <k>^(-2r))^(1/2)||h||_(H^r); the series converges for r>1/2. This proves the asserted bilinear continuity, first on polynomials and then by density. Composition in the endpoint formula, subtraction of the initial endpoint, and the inclusion to H^agamma prove continuity as used in S003.

background_notes.justification: The bilinear estimate applied to differences shows that polynomial approximations with bounded input norms give a Cauchy sequence of outputs, independent of the approximation. Completeness provides the unique extension and its bound. Truncations converge in H^gamma and thus in L2, uniformly after applying S_s because S_s is an isometry. Their products converge in L1 uniformly in s, by Cauchy-Schwarz. Pairing the differentiated products with smooth test functions and integrating over the finite step therefore identifies the limit with the distributional integral; no stronger unidentified product is used. For the power comparison, (theta-gamma)log(tau)<=0, so tau^(theta-gamma)<=1. Finally, the least-upper-bound property bounds a supremum by any common pointwise upper bound. These are the limiting and supremum steps explicitly used in S003.
